page: The Vultr voc-s-8c-64gb-1920s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance equipped with dedicated AMD EPYC x86_64 processors. It provides 8 vCPUs across 4 dedicated physical cores with symmetric multithreading enabled at a 2.0 GHz base clock speed. The processor features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, backed by instruction set extensions including AVX, AES, SHA-NI, and BMI2. The instance does not include GPU acceleration. For primary storage, it integrates 1920 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

With 64 GB of total system memory, the instance delivers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU, placing it in the memory-optimized class. Synthetic memory bandwidth benchmarks record 117.28 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 69.27 GB/sec for large-block writes. In computational workloads, the server demonstrates top-tier single-core performance in stress-ng at 3138.07, while multi-core metrics sit consistently within median industry percentiles, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 7990.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 18021.94. Data handling capabilities are solid, yielding 15.09 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 8.4 GB/sec of static web serving throughput.

The high ratio of memory and substantial local NVMe storage volume relative to core count presents an efficient hardware profile for memory-intensive and I/O-heavy environments. The primary technical tradeoff lies in its 4-core, 8-thread dedicated compute profile and lack of AVX-512 support, which limits throughput on highly parallel numerical compute and large language model inference, where 7B prompt processing delivers 18.32 tokens per second. Consequently, this server is well configured for production relational databases, Redis or Memcached caching tiers, in-memory data processing, web serving clusters, and enterprise backend applications.
description: The Vultr voc-s-8c-64gb-1920s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute virtual machine powered by dedicated AMD EPYC x86_64 architecture running at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration provides 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores, 64 GB of system memory, and a generous 1920 GB local NVMe SSD, alongside a complimentary public IPv4 address. While lacking GPU hardware and AVX-512 extensions, it achieves top-tier single-core performance in stress-ng evaluations, complemented by balanced multi-core output reflected in a 7990.0 Geekbench multi-core score. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 117.28 GB/sec, and in-memory operations achieve 15.09 million Redis SET operations per second. With an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio and direct NVMe capacity, the instance is engineered for memory-heavy and disk-dependent workloads including relational databases, caching layers, and search indexes.
